name: Vashti
title: The Deposed Queen of Persia
summary: Vashti was queen of Persia and wife to King Ahasuerus (Xerxes I). She is known for refusing to obey the king's command to appear before his guests at a great banquet, which led to her being deposed as queen. Her dismissal paved the way for Esther to become the new queen.

keyEvents.title: The King's Great Banquet
keyEvents.description: King Ahasuerus held a great banquet for all his princes and servants in Susa, the citadel, which lasted 180 days, followed by a seven-day banquet for everyone in the citadel.

keyEvents.title: Vashti's Own Banquet
keyEvents.description: While the king was holding a banquet for the men, Queen Vashti arranged her own banquet for the women in King Ahasuerus' royal palace.

keyEvents.title: Vashti Refuses the King's Command
keyEvents.description: On the seventh day, when the king was merry with wine, he commanded his seven eunuchs to bring Queen Vashti before him wearing the royal crown, so that the people and princes might see her beauty. Vashti refused to come.

keyEvents.title: The King's Wrath and the Advisors' Counsel
keyEvents.description: The king became very angry over Vashti's disobedience. His advisor Memukan recommended that a royal decree be issued stating that Vashti should never again come before the king, so that all women in the kingdom would learn to honor their husbands.

keyEvents.title: Vashti is removed as queen
keyEvents.description: The king followed the advisors' counsel, and letters were sent to all provinces stating that Vashti had been deposed. It was decided that her royal dignity should be given to another who was better than she.

keyEvents.title: The search for a new queen
keyEvents.description: After the king's anger had subsided, he remembered Vashti and what she had done. His servants suggested searching throughout the kingdom for beautiful young virgins to find a new queen, which ultimately led to Esther being chosen.
